messages:
morgan: Quick question — saw a case where private->dedicated fallback adds an extra authz roundtrip and bumps p95 by ~40ms. Anyone seen this pattern?

kai: yep. that's the authz hop: hosted control plane issues JWT -> dedicated validates with private KMS -> extra RTT. 😕

sara: can you paste any trace spans? is it a blocking call or async retry? we saw similar on big-embed workloads.

morgan: pasted trace snippet below from the canary:
```
span: request.start -> authz.fetch(aws-kms) + tcp 12ms -> token.verify 18ms -> runtime.exec
p95 latency jump correlated with authz.fetch
```

ben: hmm. sounds like 2 problems: 1) cross-hosting sync call for key material 2) synchronous verify in request path. i'd prefer async token refresh + local cache.

alex: agree. tradeoff: cache TTL vs revocation speed. for private/regulatory customers revocation must be fast. maybe make policy per-tenant: strict vs latency-optimized.

kai: +1. also worth evaluating piggybacking authz in the initial handshake so fallback doesn't require separate roundtrip. means expanding handshake payload though (bigger tokens).

sara: note: bigger tokens = larger header sizes -> a few extra bytes on every request, can blow up small-payload latency on pico-benchmarks. measure p50 cost.

morgan: proposal: 3-pronged experiment
- try local token caching with lazy async refresh (TTL=30s) for non-revokable tenants
- handshake-embed token for fallback path and measure p95
- telemetry: add span tag `authz.hops` and `authz.method` to routing traces

ben: sounds good. for telemetry add a histogram for `authz.latency` and a tag for `hosting-mode` (hosted/dedicated/private) so we can slice.

alex: devops note: if we embed tokens in handshake we must update our FCD manifest validation. @infra-bot can we get a quick check for max header size implications?

infra-bot: running quick check against egress MTU & proxy limits... will post results in thread.

sara: also flag for security review: larger handshake payload surface -> new attack vector. cc @security.

morgan: thanks. I'll open an RFC PR with the experiment matrix and add the telemetry spec. Will ping infra/security once drafted. :thumbsup:

kai: minor: ensure metrics have cardinality caps (tenant tag can explode). use coarse buckets for hosting-mode + authz.method.

morgan: noted. plan to run canary on a small set of tenants first. expected timeline: draft RFC today, canary next week.

ben: lgtm. if canary looks good, we can make handshake opt-in via deploy flag to reduce blast radius.

morgan: cool — will follow up with RFC link once ready.
